title: Alldigi Tech Ltd - 532633 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Alldigi is an HR/payroll and BPM outsourcer, not a capacity-driven business: FY26 revenue +9.6% to INR598.7 Cr, EBITDA margin 27.1%, with BPM headcount falling as management exits low-margin work and no capex expansion signalled.

summary.headline: Alldigi Tech FY26 revenue rose 9.6% to INR598.7 crore and EBITDA 25% to INR162 crore, with management guiding to mid-teens revenue growth in FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR154.7 crore (+5.9% YoY, +1.3% QoQ) and EBITDA was INR43.7 crore (+24.2% YoY), with EBITDA margin for FY26 at 27.1% versus 23.7% in FY25. Tech & Digital (T&D) was the growth engine at +22.3% YoY in Q4, while BPM was flat YoY at INR110.4 crore as management deliberately exited low-margin domestic FTE business. Management said about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin BPM business, and guided to mid-teens revenue growth and a 1-2% margin improvement for FY27. Q4 PAT rose 49.7% YoY to INR28.9 crore, and FY26 PAT was flat at INR82.2 crore. This was the first call with new CEO Natarajan Laxsmanan, who joined about a month earlier.

segments.name: Tech & Digital (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR44.3 crore (+22.3% YoY, +14.5% QoQ); FY26 revenue INR156.2 crore (+16.5%). Q4 segment margin INR19.5 crore (44%); FY26 segment margin INR66.6 crore (+28.9%). Processed 49.9 lakh employee records in Q4 and 191.5 lakh in FY26; added INR40.1 crore new ACV.

segments.name: BPM (CXM)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR110.4 crore (+0.4% YoY, flat); FY26 revenue INR442.4 crore (+7.3%). Q4 segment margin INR15 crore (about 13.6%); FY26 segment margin INR62.3 crore (+16.8%). International share of BPM revenue 78% in FY26 (73% prior year). Added INR54.1 crore new ACV; international BPM revenue grew 8.7% YoY in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens, per the CEO, similar to the aspiration stated for FY26.
EBITDA margin expected to improve about 1-2% in FY27 (management said 1-1.5% annual margin growth is typical), but no absolute margin number was given.
BPM segment margin expected to hold around 13-14%; the Q4 QoQ dip was a one-off linked to a leave policy alignment with the holding company.
T&D growth expected to be slightly higher than BPM growth; international mix expected to keep rising.
Depreciation for FY27 expected to rise only modestly (management said a couple of crore from the new Chennai office), with a sub-10% increase implied on the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.
Management expects no significant negative currency impact on revenue; a weaker rupee is expected to add to margin.
FY27 existing-customer headcount expected to be flat, with no major positive growth in employee records anticipated.
capex_capacity: Office upgrade underway in Chennai (new office being built) and Noida, with about INR20 crore of investment for the Chennai facility.
Admin and facility capex typically runs INR20-25 crore a year.
Current depreciation run-rate is about INR58.6 crore; management expects only a small increase beyond the new office.
SP4 platform migration completed for India-based customers, targeted at about INR3 crore a year in efficiency gains for T&D.
HRMS Version 2 (integrated HRMS and payroll, AI-enabled) to be released in FY27; PulseHR.ai to automate inbound query handling and cut turnaround time.
demand_pricing: HRO international order book was about 48% of total order book as of March 31, 2026 (no comparable domestic figure given).
T&D ACV wins have consistently been more than 60% from international clients.
Pipeline of large BPM brands is in place, but timing is uncertain: client decisions were on hold due to macro conditions and the war, impacting healthcare clients.
RCM (revenue cycle management) entry: processing began about a quarter ago and has doubled in FTE; further expansion with the same client is in progress.
FY27 BPM focus verticals: healthcare and RCM, international insurance, and international collections.
Existing T&D customers have plateaued; about 90% of FY26 record growth came from new customers.
Deal closure: about 30% of deals closed at CHRO/CFO level; smaller deals (under 1,000 employees) close at HR level; CEO involvement is rare.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HRO revenue grow faster than payroll-process volumes, and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue is not directly proportional to employee numbers because of one-time change requests, year-end tax work, new wage code implementation, and currency benefits from international business. Higher revenue than headcount growth is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of FY26 growth was constant currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said 3.3% of FY26 growth came from currency depreciation and 6.3% from company efforts.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BPM headcount decline continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exit from low-margin business will continue through FY27; about 10% of the portfolio is still low-margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue CAGR below the mid-teens target, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the strategic exit from low-margin business and industry factors. It still sees mid-teens growth for FY27, which it said is slightly above industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a new large BPM client and how will margins change after the exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline, citing a large pipeline and deals delayed by macro conditions. It said the low-margin exit will have minimal impact because it is only about 10% of the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why do segment margins (about INR129 crore) differ from reported EBITDA (INR162 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain said segment margins are reported at PBT level after depreciation and finance costs, net of unallocable items, other income and expenses. He offered to reconcile offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company win deals and what is the sales structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price, scale, platform flexibility, operational accuracy and turnaround time. International sales are now run by geography-specific teams with rainmaker and technology partners.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and depreciation outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Avinash Jain guided to admin/facility capex of INR20-25 crore a year plus about INR20 crore for the Chennai office, with only a small rise in depreciation from the FY26 base of about INR58.6 crore.

risks_watch: BPM growth depends on landing one or two large clients; none was onboarded in the last about 12 months, and timing is not guided.
Continued headcount decline in BPM as low-margin exits proceed; about 10% of the portfolio remains low-margin.
Flat existing-customer headcount; no major positive growth in employee records expected for FY27, so growth relies on new clients and one-time revenue.
Currency tailwind contributed about 3.3% of FY26 growth; management declined to comment on future FX effects.
AI could cut client headcounts; management called this both a challenge and an opportunity.
Segment margin reconciliation to EBITDA was not clear on the call; Vaibhav Chechani's query was left for an offline discussion.
Q4 FY26 BPM margin dip was attributed to a one-off leave policy alignment with the holding company, which is yet to be quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on T&D momentum, margins and the FY27 mid-teens growth target. Cautious and vague on BPM large-client timing, which management declined to pin to a timeline, and avoided giving absolute margin numbers.
key_quotes: And the good news is it has scaled up. It's doubled up now.
So, while there is one way of looking at it as a risk, it's also an opportunity for us.
We should -- it's -- I'm not giving you a time line, but I can give you an insight in terms of our pipeline.
So we're not anticipating any negative growth. But at the same time, we're not anticipating any major positive growth also for this year in terms of employee records.

adds.what: New Chennai office (admin/facility, ~INR20 crore investment; office upgrade underway)

growth.why: Management guides mid-teens FY27 revenue growth and 1-2% margin improvement, backed mainly by T&D momentum, RCM expansion with an existing client and international mix shift, but no specific capacity, order or contract numbers were given, so backing is partial.

mgmt.note: Natarajan Laxsmanan joined as CEO about a month before the May 2026 call and guided to mid-teens FY27 revenue growth and 1-2% margin improvement.
initiatives: BPM focus on healthcare/RCM, international insurance and collections
